thread:
Jordan: ping — got hit from acct_3b7a with a ton of 429s during a nightly backfill. customer says it started ~2026-04-10T05:10:45Z and lasted ~8m. They9re on pay-as-you-go.

Jordan: they pasted headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-burst-credits: 0
x-burst-capacity: 1500
x-burst-reset: 2026-04-10T05:18:00Z
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 10
{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"burst credits exhausted"}}
```

Lina: can you share their workload pattern? concurrency, tokens per request? cold vs warm?

Jordan: customer says: 
- kicked off ~120 concurrent workers
- each worker ~1800 tokens average per request
- sustained for ~5-7 minutes (they had a runaway requeue)
- mostly cold (new prompts)

infra-bot: org acct_3b7a metrics (last 60m): tokens: 860000; burst_allocated: 1500; burst_used: 1500; burst_remaining: 0; plan: payg.

DevOps-Chris: that math checks outmdash; sustained high concurrency with large token sizes will empty burst quickly. Default credits are for short spikes.

Lina: immediate mitigations we can offer: 1) temporary burst uplift (we can add credits for N hours) 2) enable server-side smoothing to serialize/surface concurrency 3) route to smaller model fallback for non-critical jobs 4) ask client to reduce concurrency and implement jittered retries.

Product-Alex: note for console copy: smoothing reduces hard 429s at the cost of a small median latency increase. We should highlight that in the ui next to the toggle.

Jordan: customer asked if we can do something now because their workers are stuck.

Finance-bot: suggested approval flow: for payg, CS-led temporary uplift allowed up to 25k credits/day without exec sign-off; please record ticket and cost estimate.

DevOps-Chris: propose +5k burst credits for 12h as a quick unblock and enable smoothing with a 45s window. Also set a soft-inflight limit to 100 for /v1/generate for this org.

Lina: sounds good. Chris, can you post the internal API payloads you9ll call so support can paste to customer?

DevOps-Chris: internal calls: 
```
POST /internal/orgs/acct_3b7a/burst_credits
{ "amount": 5000, "ttl_seconds": 43200, "issued_by": "devops/chris" }

PATCH /internal/orgs/acct_3b7a/config
{ "burst_smoothing": { "enabled": true, "window_seconds": 45, "max_inflight": 100 } }

PATCH /internal/orgs/acct_3b7a/routes
{ "/v1/generate": { "concurrency_limit": 100 } }
```

Jordan: deploying now. will annotate ticket TKT-6641.

Finance-bot: cost rough estimate: their recent 60m used 860k tokens. 5k credits ~5k tokens capacity; marginal infra cost around ~$0.20. CS can approve.

ops-oncall: enabling monitor: if org 429_rate > 4% over 3m alert paged. MON-ID: MON-9002. We'll also add a widget for burst_remaining.

Jordan: customer update draft: 
"We9ve applied a temporary uplift of 5,000 burst credits for 12 hours and enabled request smoothing (45s window) to reduce hard rate-limits. Please add client-side exponential backoff honoring Retry-After and limit concurrency to <=100 while we monitor. We'll follow up with an options call if you need sustained higher throughput."

Lina: sending message now. scheduling 20m check-in with the customer.

Customer-reply (pasted by Jordan): "Thanks, that cleared the 429s. We9re throttling the workers now. Could you explain smoothing in plain terms?"

Lina: quick explanation for CS: smoothing = server-side leaky bucket. requests beyond immediate capacity are queued briefly and released over a small window to avoid hitting the hard credit cap. It lowers the chance of 429s but can add ~100-400ms median delay depending on queueing. Best for background jobs.

Product-Alex: follow-up action: add a tooltip in the console that shows expected latency tradeoffs for different window sizes and a link to best-practices (client retries, batching, KV caching).

DevOps-Chris: note: if they need sustained throughput > baseline, recommend Dedicated / reserved capacity. burst credits are for short tail bursts only.

Jordan: leaving open to confirm stability for 2h. if 429s return we escalate to postmortem.

ops-oncall: ACK. I'll keep MON-9002 on watch and post updates in this thread.

Lina: nice quick win team :thumbsup:
